rules_foundation.title: 📚 LEARNING MOMENT: IoT Rules Engine
rules_foundation.content: The AWS IoT Rules Engine helps you process and route messages from your devices using SQL-like queries. Think of rules as smart filters that can send messages to different AWS services like Lambda, DynamoDB, or S3. The cool part? You can do real-time data processing and connect to your broader AWS setup without changing anything on your devices.
rules_foundation.next: Let's create and manage some IoT rules for message processing

rules_inventory.title: 📚 LEARNING MOMENT: Rules Inventory & Management
rules_inventory.content: When you list your IoT rules, you're seeing all the message processing logic that's currently running in your account. Each rule has a name, SQL statement, and actions. This gives you a clear picture of how your data flows, helps you spot unused rules, and makes it easier to manage your IoT message processing.
rules_inventory.next: Let's list all the IoT rules in your account

rule_analysis.title: 📚 LEARNING MOMENT: Rule Analysis & Troubleshooting
rule_analysis.content: Looking at a rule's details shows you everything about how it's configured - the SQL query, actions, and metadata. This is super helpful when you're troubleshooting message routing issues, trying to understand what a rule does, or checking that everything's set up the way you want.
rule_analysis.next: Let's take a closer look at a specific rule

rule_creation.title: 📚 LEARNING MOMENT: Rule Creation & Message Routing
rule_creation.content: Creating IoT rules is how you tell AWS what to do with messages from your devices. Rules use SQL-like syntax to filter and transform messages, then trigger actions like storing data, calling functions, or sending notifications. It's a powerful way to process data in real-time without touching your device code.
rule_creation.next: Let's create a new IoT rule with SQL and actions

rule_testing.title: 📚 LEARNING MOMENT: Rule Testing & Validation
rule_testing.content: Testing your rules with sample messages is a great way to make sure your SQL logic works before you go live. It helps you catch filtering mistakes, syntax errors, and logic issues that could mess up your message processing or cause unexpected behavior.
rule_testing.next: Let's test a rule with some sample MQTT messages

rule_lifecycle.title: 📚 LEARNING MOMENT: Rule Lifecycle Operations
rule_lifecycle.content: Managing rules means enabling, disabling, and deleting them as needed. When you disable a rule, it stops processing messages but keeps all the configuration. Deleting removes it for good. This kind of lifecycle management is key for keeping your IoT data processing pipeline running smoothly.
rule_lifecycle.next: Let's manage rule status and lifecycle
